findings.affected_surface: DNSSEC validation behavior for wildcard queries
findings.old_behavior: When querying for the wildcard name itself (e.g. *.example.com) and a wildcard record matches, validate_rrset() returns STAT_SECURE_WILDCARD, which triggers prove_non_existence() to check that there is no explicit record for the expanded name. This non-existence check is incorrectly performed for the wildcard name itself, potentially causing DNSSEC validation failure (BOGUS -> SERVFAIL) for legitimate wildcard queries.
findings.new_behavior: validate_rrset() now returns STAT_SECURE directly (STAT_SECURE_WILDCARD removed). The wildcard expansion status is communicated via wild_offset (int) instead of wildcard_out (char**). A new guard in validate_rrset() checks if the name is already the wildcard pattern (name_labels - labels == 1 && name_start[0] == '*' && name_start[1] == '.') and skips wildcard expansion processing. Then in dnssec_validate_reply(), when wild_offset == 0 (no wildcard expansion needed), the non-existence check via prove_non_existence() is correctly skipped, fixing the DNSSEC validation for *.example.com queries.
findings.compatibility_reason: The DNSSEC validation result for queries to the wildcard name itself (e.g. *.example.com) changes: previously could return BOGUS/SERVFAIL due to incorrect non-existence check, now correctly validates as SECURE. DNS clients and recursive resolvers behind dnsmasq may observe different responses for this specific corner case. The STAT_SECURE_WILDCARD return code has also been removed from src/dnsmasq.h, which is an internal header.

evidence.snippet:
if (verify(...))
  return STAT_SECURE;  /* was: (labels < name_labels) ? STAT_SECURE_WILDCARD : STAT_SECURE */

findings.why_not_internal_only: The change affects DNSSEC validation behavior observable by DNS clients querying through dnsmasq. A query for *.example.com that previously failed with SERVFAIL may now succeed with a valid answer, changing the DNS protocol response observable by external clients.
findings.uncertainty: The exact triggering conditions depend on DNSSEC zone configuration and whether the NSEC/NSEC3 chain happens to fail for the specific wildcard name query. This is a corner case that only affects queries for the exact wildcard name when DNSSEC validation is enabled.
findings.recommended_review: Verify the fix correctly handles: (1) wildcard queries for *.example.com with a covering wildcard record; (2) wildcard queries for a.example.com where a.example.com exists; (3) wildcard queries for non-existent a.example.com with a *.example.com wildcard. All three cases should produce correct DNSSEC validation results per RFC 4035.
findings.test_recommendation: Build dnsmasq with DNSSEC support (-DHAVE_DNSSEC). Set up a test zone with a wildcard record *.example.com. Query for *.example.com with DNSSEC validation enabled. Before the patch: may return SERVFAIL. After the patch: returns NOERROR with the wildcard answer. Also test a.example.com (exists and does not exist) to verify no regression.
